title: Psalms Chapter 49 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 49 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 49 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 49.

questions.question: In Psalms 49, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: My mouth shall speak of wisdom
I will incline mine ear to a parable
None of them can by any means redeem his brother
questions.correctAnswer: Hear this, all ye people
questions.explanation: This phrase appears in Psalms 49:1, marking the beginning of the chapter.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm for in Psalms 49?
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Korah
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:1 states it is 'A Psalm for the sons of Korah.'

questions.question: What does the speaker say he will speak of in Psalms 49?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 49:3, 'My mouth shall speak of wisdom.'

questions.question: What shall the meditation of the speaker's heart be of in Psalms 49?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:3 mentions 'the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.'

questions.question: What will the speaker do with his ear in Psalms 49?
options: Fear in the days of evil
questions.correctAnswer: Incline it to a parable
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:4 states, 'I will incline mine ear to a parable.'

questions.question: What does the speaker express fear about in Psalms 49?
questions.correctAnswer: The days of evil
questions.explanation: In Psalms 49:5, the speaker asks, 'Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 49, who cannot redeem his brother?
questions.correctAnswer: None of them
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:7 states, 'None of them can by any means redeem his brother.'

questions.question: What do those who trust in their wealth do in Psalms 49?
options: Boast themselves in the multitude of their riches
Fear in the days of evil
Incline their ear to a parable
questions.correctAnswer: Boast themselves in the multitude of their riches
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:6 states, 'They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches.'

questions.question: What is the speaker's response to the iniquity surrounding him in Psalms 49?
questions.correctAnswer: He will not fear
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:5 suggests that the speaker questions why he should fear, indicating he will not fear.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the speaker's dark saying in Psalms 49?
options: To open it upon the harp
questions.correctAnswer: To open it upon the harp
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:4 mentions, 'I will open my dark saying upon the harp.'

questions.question: What does the Psalm address in Psalms 49:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Both low and high
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:2 states, 'Both low and high, rich and poor, together.'

questions.question: The statement 'I will open my dark saying upon the harp' is found in which verse?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is found in Psalms 49:4.

questions.question: Psalms 49 states that rich and poor are addressed together.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 49:2, where both rich and poor are mentioned together.

questions.question: The speaker claims to fear the iniquity of the rich.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The speaker questions why he should fear, indicating he does not fear iniquity, as stated in Psalms 49:5.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49, wealth can redeem one's brother.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:7 explicitly states that 'None of them can by any means redeem his brother.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 49 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 49 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49:8, what is described as precious and ceaseth forever?
questions.correctAnswer: The redemption of their soul
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:8 states that the redemption of their soul is precious and it ceaseth forever, emphasizing the value of salvation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 49:9 promise will happen if someone truly redeems their soul as stated in Psalms 49:8?
options: That he should still live forever, and not see corruption
That he will gain great riches
That he will build houses that last forever
That he will be honored by all people
questions.correctAnswer: That he should still live forever, and not see corruption
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:9 follows Psalms 49:8 by promising that the one who redeems his soul will live forever and not see corruption.

questions.question: What observation does Psalms 49:10 make about the fate of wise men, fools, and brutish persons?
options: They die and leave their wealth to others
They build houses that last forever
They are honored by God above all
questions.correctAnswer: They die and leave their wealth to others
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:10 explains that wise men, fools, and brutish persons all perish and leave their wealth to others, showing the common destiny of death.

questions.question: How do Psalms 49:11 and Psalms 49:12 contrast human expectations and reality?
options: People think their houses and lands will last forever, but man abides not and is like the beasts that perish
People know they will perish, but they still boast of their riches
People live forever, but their wealth perishes
People trust God, yet their possessions vanish
questions.correctAnswer: People think their houses and lands will last forever, but man abides not and is like the beasts that perish
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:11 shows people’s inward thought that their houses and lands shall continue forever, but Psalms 49:12 corrects this by stating man does not abide and is like beasts that perish.

questions.question: What is the folly mentioned in Psalms 49:13 regarding human ways?
options: Their way is folly even though their posterity approve their sayings
Their way is wise and leads to eternal life
Their way is to trust in God alone
Their way is to give to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Their way is folly even though their posterity approve their sayings
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:13 states that their way is folly, yet their posterity approve their sayings, showing a generational acceptance of error.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49:14, what happens to people like sheep when they die?
options: They are laid in the grave and death feeds on them
They live forever in their homes
They ascend to the heavens immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They are laid in the grave and death feeds on them
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:14 compares people to sheep laid in the grave, with death feeding on them, illustrating the inevitability of death.

questions.question: In Psalms 49:10-11, what misconception do people have about their wealth and property?
options: They believe their houses and lands will continue forever and bear their names
They know their wealth will perish with them
They give all their possessions to the poor
They trust God for eternal life rather than riches
questions.correctAnswer: They believe their houses and lands will continue forever and bear their names
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:11 highlights that people think their houses will last forever and their lands will bear their names through generations.

questions.question: What practical lesson about life and death can Christians learn from Psalms 49:12?
options: Despite honor, man does not abide and is like beasts that perish, so reliance on earthly status is futile
questions.correctAnswer: Despite honor, man does not abide and is like beasts that perish, so reliance on earthly status is futile
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:12 teaches that human honor is temporary and mortality equalizes man and beasts, urging faith beyond worldly status.

questions.question: How does Psalms 49:14 describe the fate of the upright compared to the wicked after death?
options: The upright shall have dominion over the wicked in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: The upright shall have dominion over the wicked in the morning
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:14 promises that though all die, the upright will have dominion over the wicked after death.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49:8-9, why is the redemption of the soul considered valuable?
options: Because it leads to eternal life without seeing corruption
Because it brings wealth and honor
Because it allows building lasting houses
questions.correctAnswer: Because it leads to eternal life without seeing corruption
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:8-9 link the preciousness of soul redemption to the promise of living forever and not experiencing decay.

questions.question: What warning does Psalms 49:6-7 imply about trusting in wealth?
options: Those who trust in riches cannot redeem their brother or ransom themselves before God
Trusting in wealth leads to building everlasting homes
questions.correctAnswer: Those who trust in riches cannot redeem their brother or ransom themselves before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:6-7 teach that trusting in wealth is futile because no one can ransom a brother or give a ransom to God with riches.

questions.question: How might Psalms 49:10-12 influence a Christian's attitude toward material possessions?
options: It encourages focusing on eternal matters rather than earthly wealth since all die and perish
It advises accumulating wealth for future generations
It suggests building houses that last forever
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages focusing on eternal matters rather than earthly wealth since all die and perish
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:10-12 highlight death's certainty and the temporary nature of possessions, urging believers to prioritize eternal life.

questions.question: What does Psalms 49:13 suggest about the influence of human folly across generations?
options: That folly is passed down and approved by future generations despite being foolish
That only the wise influence future generations
questions.correctAnswer: That folly is passed down and approved by future generations despite being foolish
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:13 states that though their way is folly, their posterity approve their sayings, showing how error can be perpetuated.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 49:14 states that death will consume the beauty of the upright in the grave.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:14 says the beauty of the upright shall consume in the grave from their dwelling, confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 49:9, the person who redeems their soul will eventually see corruption.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:9 states that the person who redeems their soul shall not see corruption, making the statement false.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 49 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 49.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49:15, what will God do for the psalmist's soul?
options: God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave
God will grant me long life on earth
God will give me a large family
questions.correctAnswer: God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:15 states, 'But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me.' This clearly indicates God's redeeming action for the soul.

questions.question: What instruction is given in Psalms 49:16 regarding those who become rich?
options: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich
Envy the rich and seek to be like them
Trust only in your own riches
Ignore the poor and focus on the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:16 says, 'Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;' instructing not to fear the increase of another’s wealth.

questions.question: What does Psalms 49:17 say about what a rich man carries after death?
options: He shall carry his wealth to the grave
He shall carry his glory to his children
He shall carry his house to the next generation
questions.correctAnswer: He shall carry nothing away
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:17 states, 'For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him,' indicating the futility of earthly possessions after death.

questions.question: According to Psalms 49:18, how do men respond when someone does well for himself?
questions.correctAnswer: Men will praise thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:18 says, 'and men will praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself,' indicating that people praise those who prosper.

questions.question: What happens to a man who is in honour but lacks understanding according to Psalms 49:20?
options: He is like the beasts that perish
He is wiser than the elders
questions.correctAnswer: He is like the beasts that perish
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:20 declares, 'Man that is in honour, and understandeth not, is like the beasts that perish,' emphasizing the futility of honour without understanding.

questions.question: What is the ultimate destiny of those who die rich as described in Psalms 49:19?
options: They shall go to the generation of their fathers; they shall never see light
They shall ascend to heaven immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They shall go to the generation of their fathers; they shall never see light
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:19 states, 'He shall go to the generation of his fathers; they shall never see light,' indicating death leads to darkness regardless of wealth.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ga'al' in Psalms 49:15 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To redeem or ransom
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ga'al' (גָּאַל) used in Psalms 49:15 means 'to redeem or ransom,' referring to God's action to redeem the soul from the grave.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 49:17-18 contrasting wealth and death?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:17-18 contrasts the increase of wealth with the inevitability of death, an example of antithesis, a literary device that juxtaposes contrasting ideas.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the futility of earthly riches found in Psalms 49:6-7?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Timothy 6:17-19
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:17-19 warns the rich not to be arrogant or to trust in wealth, echoing Psalms 49:6-7 which states that wealth cannot redeem a brother.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of death's dominion over man as stated in Psalms 49:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Ecclesiastes 3:20
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:20 states that all go to one place—death—aligning with Psalms 49:14 where death feeds on the dead, showing death's dominion over man.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Psalms 49:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 49:14
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:14 directly precedes 49:15 according to the chapter sequence and discusses people laid in the grave, setting the context for verse 15's redemption theme.

questions.question: How does Psalms 49:12 relate man in honour to beasts?
options: Man in honour abideth not; he is like the beasts that perish
Man in honour is superior to beasts
Man in honour controls the beasts
Man in honour lives forever unlike beasts
questions.correctAnswer: Man in honour abideth not; he is like the beasts that perish
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:12 states, 'Nevertheless man being in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish,' emphasizing mortality despite honour.

questions.question: What is the folly of those who trust in wealth according to Psalms 49:13?
options: Their way is folly though their posterity approve their sayings
Their wealth will secure eternal life
Their riches will protect them from death
questions.correctAnswer: Their way is folly though their posterity approve their sayings
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:13 explains that trusting in wealth is folly, even if their descendants agree with their views, highlighting the shortsightedness of such trust.

questions.question: What typological foreshadowing is found in Psalms 49:15 regarding redemption from the grave?
options: It foreshadows Christ's resurrection and redemption
It predicts the building of Solomon's temple
It symbolizes the Exodus out of Egypt
It indicates the rise of the Davidic monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's resurrection and redemption
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:15's promise that God will redeem the soul from the grave prefigures the New Testament theme of Christ's resurrection and redemption from death.

questions.question: How does Psalms 49:10 use parallelism to express the fate of both wise and foolish men?
options: It parallels wise men dying and fools perishing, showing equality in death
It contrasts the eternal life of wise men with the death of fools
It uses metaphor to depict men as trees
It personifies death as a merciful friend
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels wise men dying and fools perishing, showing equality in death
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:10 employs synonymous parallelism stating both wise and fools die and perish, emphasizing death’s impartiality.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 49 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 49 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 49:7 teach about human sin and salvation?
options: No one can redeem another by wealth or ransom before God
Wealth increases one's ability to secure salvation
Ransom payments can guarantee eternal life
Humans can earn redemption through good deeds
questions.correctAnswer: No one can redeem another by wealth or ransom before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:7 states, 'None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him,' emphasizing the doctrine that human wealth cannot secure salvation or redemption for others.

questions.question: What doctrine about human mortality does Psalms 49:10 teach?
options: Both wise and foolish persons die and leave their wealth behind
Only the foolish perish, while the wise live forever
Wealth protects one from death and corruption
The righteous are exempt from physical death
questions.correctAnswer: Both wise and foolish persons die and leave their wealth behind
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:10 says, 'For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others,' showing that death is the common destiny regardless of wisdom or folly.

questions.question: What doctrine about the futility of earthly riches is taught in Psalms 49:16?
options: Riches cannot be taken after death and do not provide lasting glory
Wealth is a sign of God's eternal favor
Accumulating wealth guarantees a place in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Riches cannot be taken after death and do not provide lasting glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:16 warns, 'Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased,' teaching that wealth is temporal and does not endure beyond death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 49:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Redemptive power
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:15 declares, 'But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave,' showing God's attribute of redemptive power over death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 49:6 regarding human trust?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over human pride
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:6 speaks of those who 'trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches,' implying God's sovereignty over human arrogance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 49 prepare for the New Testament teaching on the resurrection and eternal life?
options: By contrasting death's dominion with God's power to redeem the soul
By promising wealth to the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting death's dominion with God's power to redeem the soul
questions.explanation: The chapter contrasts death's power over all people with God's redeeming power (Psalms 49:14-15), which foreshadows New Testament resurrection hope (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:54-55).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Psalms 49:12 establish regarding human nature?
options: Man is like the beasts that perish despite his honor
Man is inherently divine and immortal
questions.correctAnswer: Man is like the beasts that perish despite his honor
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:12 compares man with beasts that perish, emphasizing human mortality and the need for divine redemption, a theme developed in biblical anthropology (cf. Ecclesiastes 3:19).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 49:7 and 49:15 teach about salvation?
options: Human wealth cannot redeem, but God redeems the soul from death
Both human effort and divine power equally secure salvation
Ransom payments are the primary means of redemption
Salvation depends solely on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Human wealth cannot redeem, but God redeems the soul from death
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:7 denies human ransom power, while 49:15 affirms God's redeeming power, combining to teach salvation is solely by divine grace.

questions.question: What doctrine about the vanity of earthly confidence is taught by Psalms 49:11 and 49:17 together?
options: Human plans for lasting legacy and glory are ultimately futile
questions.correctAnswer: Human plans for lasting legacy and glory are ultimately futile
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows people presume their houses and lands endure forever, while verse 17 states that glory does not descend after death, highlighting earthly futility.

questions.question: What theological synthesis arises from Psalms 49:20 and 49:12 about human understanding and mortality?
options: Man in honor but without understanding is like beasts that perish, underscoring human mortality and folly
Beasts are immortal due to lack of understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Man in honor but without understanding is like beasts that perish, underscoring human mortality and folly
questions.explanation: Both verses stress that honor without insight offers no escape from death, equating such humans to perishing animals.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 49:8-9 teaches humans can live forever through their own efforts. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The passage states that redemption of the soul is precious and humans do not live forever or avoid corruption
It promises eternal life to those who accumulate wealth
It supports reincarnation as a means to avoid corruption
questions.correctAnswer: The passage states that redemption of the soul is precious and humans do not live forever or avoid corruption
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 clarify that no one lives forever or escapes decay, emphasizing the preciousness of redemption rather than human self-sufficiency.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 49:13 teach about the folly of trusting in riches?
options: Trusting in riches is folly, yet descendants often approve such folly
Wealth is a sure sign of divine favor
The folly of riches is quickly forgotten by future generations
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in riches is folly, yet descendants often approve such folly
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:13 states, 'This their way is their folly: yet their posterity approve their sayings,' showing a generational perpetuation of mistaken trust in wealth.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the psalmist's declaration in Psalms 49:3 about speaking wisdom and understanding?
options: God's gift of wisdom and revelation
questions.correctAnswer: God's gift of wisdom and revelation
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:3 says, 'My mouth shall speak of wisdom; and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding,' reflecting divine gifting of wisdom for instruction.

questions.question: What theological theme emerges from Psalms 49:14 and 49:18 concerning death and human legacy?
options: Death consumes beauty and glory, and earthly blessings do not follow after death
Death is a doorway to increased glory
Human beauty and blessings are eternal
After death, wealth increases in value
questions.correctAnswer: Death consumes beauty and glory, and earthly blessings do not follow after death
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes death consuming beauty, and verse 18 notes that men praise while alive but do not carry blessings beyond death.

questions.question: How does Psalms 49:4 use divine inspiration to reveal hidden truths to the faithful?
options: The psalmist opens a dark saying upon the harp, symbolizing God’s revelation through inspired song
Truths are revealed only through dreams
The harp signifies human wisdom without divine help
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist opens a dark saying upon the harp, symbolizing God’s revelation through inspired song
questions.explanation: Psalms 49:4 says, 'I will open my dark saying upon the harp,' indicating inspired revelation communicated through music and poetry.
